HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P) NOTE  

History:  
• Chief complaint: Sudden inability to move left arm upon awakening this morning (≈1 hour prior to call).  
• Onset/Duration: Acute onset on waking; symptoms persistent.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Tingling on left side of face since onset.  
  – Dysphagia (“spilled drink,” difficulty swallowing).  
  – Dysarthria (speech slower, harder to produce).  
• Negatives: No left-leg symptoms, no arm pain, no discoloration or coldness of hand, patient notes no obvious facial asymmetry.  
• Context: Slept in normal position, no recent trauma or illness. First episode. Lives alone.

Past Medical History:  
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus.  
• Hypertension.  
• Family history: Father with heart disease.  
• Social: Former smoker; drinks several pints of beer on weekends and a few during the week. Lives alone.  
• Allergies: Penicillin (reaction not specified).  
• Current medications:  
  – Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  – Losartan – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  – Amlodipine – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Physical Examination (teleconsult – patient-reported findings):  
• General: Alert, conversational via phone.  
• Neurologic: Unable to move left arm; tingling left facial area; slowed/slurred speech; difficulty swallowing liquids. No reported left-leg weakness.  
• Extremities: No pain, discoloration, or coldness in left arm/hand.  
• Airway/Respiratory: No reports of dyspnea.  
• Mental status: Oriented; able to follow instructions.

Impression:  
• Suspected acute cerebrovascular event (stroke) – left-sided upper-limb weakness with facial paresthesia, dysphagia, and dysarthria.

Management Plan:  
• Emergency services (999) activated; ambulance dispatched to patient’s home.  
• Patient instructed to unlock front door and sit in hallway for access.  
• Physician remained on line until ambulance arrival.  
• Anticipated hospital evaluation in ED with urgent stroke team review and imaging ± thrombolysis as indicated.  
• No additional outpatient management initiated.

Patient Summary:  
Mr. Jack Armani (DOB 12 Aug 1958) awoke unable to move his left arm, with left facial tingling, dysphagia, and dysarthria—highly suggestive of an acute stroke. Emergency transport arranged for immediate hospital assessment and treatment.

Key Takeaways for Patient:  
1. Ambulance is en route; unlock door and wait seated nearby.  
2. Remain on phone with clinician until paramedics arrive.  
3. Hospital team will perform urgent scans and possible clot-busting therapy.

Next Steps:  
• ED/stroke team assessment with brain imaging (CT/MRI) and labs.  
• Determine eligibility for thrombolysis or thrombectomy.  
• In-hospital monitoring and secondary prevention planning.  
• Primary care follow-up after discharge for BP, diabetes, and risk-factor management.

Quality checks (document_quality):  
• Missing elements: Objective vital signs, full neurological exam, medication dosages and frequencies.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; no significant audio gaps.
